items.summary: As more of a person’s life moves online, a need has emerged to address what happens when an individual dies or is unable to access their digital data due to incapacity. India’s new data protection law attempts to address this through the nomination right but leaves gaps that a data fiduciary must fill to comply with the legislation's objectives. Section 14(1) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“ DP Act ”) allows an individual, the data principal, to nominate any other person who may, on the data principal’s death or incapacity, exercise that individual’s statutory rights under the DP Act and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (“ DP Rules ”). The Act grants the nominee broad authority to exercise powers as if stepping into the shoes of the data principal. Does the right to nominate fill the gap it was designed to fill? The gap the provision attempts to fill is genuine, but the machinery to operate it is thin.
